papers.title: Organizing across cognitive asymmetry in human–AI collaboration: A study of perfume creation
papers.abstract: As organizations increasingly adopt generative AI (GenAI), they face a strategic challenge: not only deciding which tasks AI should perform, but also how to organize the integration of human and AI efforts to produce viable solutions. We propose that a cognitive asymmetry between human's tacit, embodied knowledge and AI's codified knowledge creates a representational gap that complicates human–GenAI collaboration. Through a qualitative study of professional perfume creation, we identify three organizational mechanisms—boundary-spanning routines, representational translation, and emergent role differentiation—that help organizations bridge this gap and coordinate human–AI collaboration toward viable creative outcomes.
papers.summary_ja: 生成AIと人間の協働における認知的非対称性（暗黙知vs.コード化知識）が引き起こす「表現ギャップ」を特定し、境界スパニング・ルーティン、表現翻訳、役割分化という3つの組織メカニズムによって克服できることをパフューム創作の事例研究で実証した。

papers.title: Cultivating institutional imagination through service design: speculating on alternative logics in the Estonian mental health service ecosystem
papers.abstract: This article aims to investigate how service design can aid actors in cultivating institutional imagination – their ability to speculate on alternative constellations of widely shared and entrenched logics in service ecosystems. This study applies a research-through-design approach involving 25 generative interviews, 2 co-creation workshops with 23 system actors, and 2 reflection sessions with 25 system actors in the Estonian mental healthcare service ecosystem. Service design tools enabled actors to externalize and reframe institutionalized logics, facilitating the imagination of alternative service configurations.
papers.summary_ja: サービスデザインが「制度的想像力」——既存のサービスエコシステムの論理を問い直し、代替的な構成を思考する能力——の育成をいかに支援するかを、エストニアのメンタルヘルス・サービスエコシステムにおける研究-through-デザインアプローチで実証した。

papers.title: When humans stop thinking: tackling the silent threat of AI complacency in service operations
papers.authors: Khanh Bao Quang Le et al.
papers.abstract: This research investigates the phenomenon of AI complacency – the employee's tendency to intentionally neglect validating AI-generated output even in the presence of systematic errors. It identifies the lack of monitoring accountability as the underlying driver of this phenomenon, assesses its consequences, and offers strategies for mitigation. Grounded in contingency theory, this research employs six experimental studies (N = 1,370 participants), including online experiments, vignette studies, and a field experiment, to demonstrate that AI complacency degrades service quality and customer satisfaction.
papers.summary_ja: AIが生成したアウトプットの検証を従業員が意図的に怠る「AIコンプレイアンシー（AI依存性怠慢）」を6つの実験（N=1,370）で実証し、モニタリング責任の欠如が主因であり、サービス品質と顧客満足度を著しく低下させることを示した。

papers.title: Configurational pathways to professional service innovation: a fuzzy set analysis of provider adoption decisions
papers.abstract: This study investigates how healthcare professionals make complex adoption decisions that transform service encounters and value co-creation processes. While most research has focused on patient-side technology adoption, this study advances the understanding of the configurational conditions that drive provider-side adoption of digital service innovations. Employing fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study analyzes data from 315 self-employed healthcare professionals to identify equifinal paths to innovation adoption.
papers.summary_ja: 医療専門職315名のfsQCAデータ分析により、デジタルサービスイノベーションの提供者側採用を促す複数の等結果的（equifinal）構成条件経路を特定し、患者中心の視点に偏りがちな従来研究を提供者側の意思決定構造から補完した。

papers.title: Agentic AI as a service innovation: A mixed-methods study of satisfaction, trust, and continued use
papers.abstract: AI agents and agentic AI systems are increasingly employed for decision-making and task execution. However, limited evidence explains how users evaluate agentic features or form intentions to continue using these systems. This gap has important implications for service innovation and innovation management, because sustained adoption determines whether agentic AI generates scalable value in real use. This study examines how perceived agentic characteristics—autonomy, proactivity, goal-directedness—shape user satisfaction, trust, and continued use intentions through a mixed-methods study.
papers.summary_ja: エージェント型AI（自律性・能動性・目標指向性）のサービスイノベーションとしての採用を混合研究法で検証し、ユーザー満足度・信頼・継続利用意図に対してエージェント特性がどのように機能するかを解明した。

papers.title: Dynamic capabilities in business ecosystem emergence: a marketing technology case study
papers.abstract: This article examines how dynamic capabilities (DC) evolve during the emergence of a business ecosystem. It addresses how sensing, seizing and transforming activities take shape, change character and become distributed as value creation increasingly depends on coordination among interdependent actors. The study draws on a longitudinal, inductive case of Odins.ai, a Norwegian marketing technology company whose value creation model relies on collaboration with complementors and platform participants.
papers.summary_ja: ノルウェーのマーケティングテクノロジー企業の縦断的事例研究を通じて、ビジネスエコシステムの発生過程でダイナミック・ケイパビリティ（感知・把握・変革）がどのように進化・分散化していくかを解明した。

papers.title: Global brains: the science and practice of collective intelligence at the level of whole systems
papers.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: What is the science and practice of collective intelligence at the level of whole systems and at a global scale? How have attempts to organize intelligence at these scales evolved, and how might they evolve in the future? Recent research has attempted to find universal patterns in the organization of intelligence at multiple scales, from atoms and cells to birds and other animals and whole societies. This work offers insights for the design of intelligence at global scales that can support governance, policy and social innovation.
papers.summary_ja: 個人・組織・社会・地球規模における集合知の科学と実践を統合的にレビューし、複数スケールで知性を組織するための普遍的パターンを探索、グローバルガバナンスや社会イノベーションへの設計的示唆を提示した。

papers.title: Understanding the Global Trends of 2025 Through the Defly Compass Methodology
papers.abstract: This study aims to identify and synthesize the major global trends that shaped 2025 by applying the DeflyCompass methodology to a curated corpus of strategic foresight reports. The study synthesizes insights from 23 strategic reports published by leading international organizations, including the World Economic Forum, Accenture, Euromonitor, and major technology firms. Methodologically, DeflyCompass operationalizes a structured hybrid human–AI pipeline comprising the deployment of multi-agent AI systems to analyze and synthesize large volumes of foresight data.
papers.summary_ja: WEF・Accenture等23機関の戦略的フォーサイトレポートをマルチエージェントAIを活用したDeflyCompass手法で分析し、2025年の主要グローバルトレンドを体系的に特定・統合する新しいハイブリッド人間-AIパイプラインを提示した。

papers.title: Can GenAI Move from Individual Use to Collaborative Work? Experiences, Challenges, and Opportunities of Coordinating GenAI into Collaborative Newswork
papers.journal: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping work, but adoption remains largely individual and experimental rather than coordinated into collaborative work. Whether GenAI can move from individual use to collaborative work is a critical question for future organizations. Journalism offers a compelling site to examine this shift: individual journalists have already been disrupted by GenAI tools; yet newswork is inherently collaborative relying on shared norms and coordinated workflows. We conducted 27 interviews with journalists and editors to investigate how GenAI is being integrated into collaborative newswork.
papers.summary_ja: ジャーナリズムを事例に27名へのインタビューを通じて、生成AIが個人利用から組織的協働ワークへと移行する際の課題・機会・調整メカニズムを明らかにし、組織でのGenAI統合設計に示唆を与えた。

papers.title: Better together: mitigating consumer vulnerability risk in healthcare systems through strengthening consumer co-production capacity
papers.abstract: Consumer vulnerability risk in co-production emerges from unequal power relations and exclusionary partnerships in services. Consumer experiential knowledge must be recognised, valued, leveraged, and rewarded for partnership-based co-production. Practices for strengthening consumer co-production capacity acknowledge and address power imbalances and relations. Service scholars tacitly assume that healthcare consumers, professionals, and researchers possess the requisite capacities and resources to co-produce and innovate services together.
papers.summary_ja: 医療サービスの共同生産（co-production）における消費者の脆弱性リスクが不平等なパワー関係から生じることを示し、消費者の経験的知識を認識・活用・報酬化する共同生産能力強化のための実践的フレームワークを提示した。
